newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cell phone, PC output forecast raised.
newsitem.headline: Japan cell phone, PC output forecast raised.

text.p: The Electronic Industries Association of Japan (EIAJ) said on Thursday it had raised its forecast for output of electronics goods for industrial use, including cellular phones and personal computers, for calendar 1996.
But the EIAJ said it now expects that Japan's output in 1996 of consumer electronics goods, such as colour television sets, and electronics parts and devices, to be lower than in 1995.
In December 1995, it said output would be higher in 1996 than in 1995.
The EIAJ expects Japan's output of industrial-use electronics goods in 1996 to increase 15.3 percent from a year ago, against its previous forecast of a year-on-year 3.7 percent rise.
The upward revision is due to active production of mobile phones, including those using the personal handyphone system (PHS) and PCs, the EIAJ said.
The phones are classified as industrial-use electronics goods.
The EIAJ sees Japan's output of electronics goods for consumers falling by 9.9 percent in 1996, against its previous forecast of a year-on-year rise of 1.7 percent.
It sees output of electronics parts and devices falling by 1.0 percent in 1996, against its previous forecast of a year-on-year rise of 8.9 percent.
As a result of the revisions, EIAJ expects Japan's production of overall electronics goods in 1996 to rise 5.7 percent, up from its previous forecast of a rise of 5.6 percent.
In 1995, Japan's production of overall electronics goods was up 5.9 percent from the year before, the EIAJ said.
